units.translation: for a woman to sit in the house without a man, desolate, is a terrible evil.
ἐρῆμος [desolate]: no word ending in -μος of more than two syllables with circumflex on the penult has η in the penult, except ἐρῆμος [desolate]
as he saw the desolate place. The Attic writers, however, accent the word on the antepenult
and this too, they say, is accented on the antepenult by the later Attic writers
Herodian says that the Homeric ἐρῆμον [desolate] and ἑτοῖμον [ready] are said by the later Attic writers, by analogy, as ἔρημον [desolate] and ἕτοιμον [ready]

Thus Seidler corrected for ἐρικύματα [bearing many offspring], which is in M, changed in the copies to ἐρικύμονα [bearing many offspring]. Similar is ἀρικύμων [easily conceiving] said by Hippocrates of a woman who conceives easily. As to the form of the word, compare παιδολυμάς [destroying children], which see.

(The correct spelling Ἐρινύς [Erinys] is attested by grammarians and examples of inscriptions and for the most part preserved by the older manuscripts of writers, among them the Laurentian of Aeschylus and Sophocles, in later ones often corrupted to Ἐριννύς [Erinnys]: on which see the Thesaurus vol. 3 p. 2023).
